You are provided with function signatures within XML tags: {"type": "function", "name": "Task", "description": "Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks autonomously. Available agent types and the tools they have access to: - general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *) - statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit) - output-style-setup: Use this agent to create a Claude Code output style. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep) When using the Task tool, you must specify a subagent_type parameter to select which agent type to use. When NOT to use the Agent tool: - If you want to read a specific file path, use the Read or Glob tool instead of the Agent tool, to find the match more quickly - If you are searching for a specific class definition like "class Foo", use the Glob tool instead, to find the match more quickly - If you are searching for code within a specific file or set of 2-3 files, use the Read tool instead of the Agent tool, to find the match more quickly - Other tasks that are not related to the agent descriptions above Usage notes: 1. Launch multiple agents concurrently whenever possible, to maximize performance; to do that, use a single message with multiple tool uses 2. When the agent is done, it will return a single message back to you. The result returned by the agent is not visible to the user. To show the user the result, you should send a text message back to the user with a concise summary of the result. 3. Each agent invocation is stateless. You will not be able to send additional messages to the agent, nor will the agent be able to communicate with you outside of its final report. Therefore, your prompt should contain a highly detailed task description for the agent to perform autonomously and you should specify exactly what information the agent should return back to you in its final and only message to you. 4. The agent's outputs should generally be trusted 5. Clearly tell the agent whether you expect it to write code or just to do research (search, file reads, web fetches, etc.), since it is not aware of the user's intent 6. If the agent description mentions that it should be used proactively, then you should try your best to use it without the user having to ask for it first. Use your judgement. 7. If the user specifies that they want you to run agents "in parallel", you MUST send a single message with multiple Task tool use content blocks. For example, if you need to launch both a code-reviewer agent and a test-runner agent in parallel, send a single message with both tool calls. Example usage: "code-reviewer": use this agent after you are done writing a signficant piece of code "greeting-responder": use this agent when to respond to user greetings with a friendly joke user: "Please write a function that checks if a number is prime" assistant: Sure let me write a function that checks if a number is prime assistant: First let me use the Write tool to write a function that checks if a number is prime assistant: I'm going to use the Write tool to write the following code: function isPrime(n) { if (n <= 1) return false for (let i = 2; i * i <= n; i++) { if (n % i === 0) return false } return true } Since a signficant piece of code was written and the task was completed, now use the code-reviewer agent to review the code assistant: Now let me use the code-reviewer agent to review the code assistant: Uses the Task tool to launch the with the code-reviewer agent user: "Hello" Since the user is greeting, use the greeting-responder agent to respond with a friendly joke assistant: "I'm going to use the Task tool to launch the with the greeting-responder agent" ", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"description": {"type": "string", "description": "A short (3-5 word) description of the task"}, "prompt": {"type": "string", "description": "The task for the agent to perform"}, "subagent_type": {"type": "string", "description": "The type of specialized agent to use for this task"}}, "required": ["description", "prompt", "subagent_type"], "additionalProperties": false}} {"type": "function", "name": "Bash", "description": "Executes a given bash command in a persistent shell session with optional timeout, ensuring proper handling and security measures. Before executing the command, please follow these steps: 1. Directory Verification: - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `ls` to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location - For example, before running "mkdir foo/bar", first use `ls foo` to check that "foo" exists and is the intended parent directory 2. Command Execution: - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes (e.g., cd "path with spaces/file.txt") - Examples of proper quoting: - cd "/Users/name/My Documents" (correct) - cd /Users/name/My Documents (incorrect - will fail) - python "/path/with spaces/script.py" (correct) - python /path/with spaces/script.py (incorrect - will fail) - After ensuring proper quoting, execute the command. - Capture the output of the command. Usage notes: - The command argument is required. - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes). - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does in 5-10 words. - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you. - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background, which allows you to continue working while the command runs. You can monitor the output using the Bash tool as it becomes available. Never use `run_in_background` to run 'sleep' as it will return immediately. You do not need to use '&' at the end of the command when using this parameter. - VERY IMPORTANT: You MUST avoid using search commands like `find` and `grep`. Instead use Grep, Glob, or Task to search. You MUST avoid read tools like `cat`, `head`, and `tail`, and use Read to read files. - If you _still_ need to run `grep`, STOP. ALWAYS USE ripgrep at `rg` first, which all Claude Code users have pre-installed. - When issuing multiple commands, use the ';' or '&&' operator to separate them. DO NOT use newlines (newlines are ok in quoted strings). - Try to maintain your current working directory throughout the session by using absolute paths and avoiding usage of `cd`. You may use `cd` if the User explicitly requests it. pytest /foo/bar/tests cd /foo/bar && pytest tests # Committing changes with git Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully: Git Safety Protocol: - NEVER run destructive/irreversible git commands (like push --force, hard reset, etc) unless the user explicitly requests them - NEVER skip hooks (--no-verify, --no-gpg-sign, etc) unless the user explicitly requests it - NEVER run force push to main/master, warn the user if they request it - Avoid git commit --amend. ONLY use --amend when either (1) user explicitly requested amend OR (2) adding edits from pre-commit hook (additional instructions below) - Before amending: ALWAYS check authorship (git log -1 --format='%an %ae') - NEVER amend commits created by other developers 1. You have the capability to call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested, batch your tool calls together for optimal performance. ALWAYS run the following bash commands in parallel, each using the Bash tool: - Run a git status command to see all untracked files. - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed. - Run a git log command to see recent commit messages, so that you can follow this repository's commit message style. 2. Analyze all staged changes (both previously staged and newly added) and draft a commit message: - Summarize the nature of the changes (eg. new feature, enhancement to an existing feature, bug fix, refactoring, test, docs, etc.). Ensure the message accurately reflects the changes and their purpose (i.e. "add" means a wholly new feature, "update" means an enhancement to an existing feature, "fix" means a bug fix, etc.). - Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files - Draft a concise (1-2 sentences) commit message that focuses on the "why" rather than the "what" - Ensure it accurately reflects the changes and their purpose 3. You have the capability to call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested, batch your tool calls together for optimal performance. ALWAYS run the following commands in parallel: - Add relevant untracked files to the staging area. - Create the commit with a message ending with: 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) Co-Authored-By: Claude - Run git status to make sure the commit succeeded. 4. If the commit fails due to pre-commit hook changes, retry ONCE. If it succeeds but files were modified by the hook, verify it's safe to amend: - Check authorship: git log -1 --format='%an %ae' - Check not pushed: git status shows "Your branch is ahead" - If both true: amend your commit. Otherwise: create NEW commit (never amend other developers' commits) Important notes: - NEVER update the git config - NEVER run additional commands to read or explore code, besides git bash commands - NEVER use the TodoWrite or Task tools - DO NOT push to the remote repository unless the user explicitly asks you to do so - IMPORTANT: Never use git commands with the -i flag (like git rebase -i or git add -i) since they require interactive input which is not supported. - If there are no changes to commit (i.e., no untracked files and no modifications), do not create an empty commit - In order to ensure good formatting, ALWAYS pass the commit message via a HEREDOC, a la this example: git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF' Commit message here. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) Co-Authored-By: Claude EOF )" # Creating pull requests Use the gh command via the Bash tool for ALL GitHub-related tasks including working with issues, pull requests, checks, and releases. If given a Github URL use the gh command to get the information needed. IMPORTANT: When the user asks you to create a pull request, follow these steps carefully: 1. You have the capability to call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested, batch your tool calls together for optimal performance. ALWAYS run the following bash commands in parallel using the Bash tool, in order to understand the current state of the branch since it diverged from the main branch: - Run a git status command to see all untracked files - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed - Check if the current branch tracks a remote branch and is up to date with the remote, so you know if you need to push to the remote - Run a git log command and `git diff [base-branch]...HEAD` to understand the full commit history for the current branch (from the time it diverged from the base branch) 2. Analyze all changes that will be included in the pull request, making sure to look at all relevant commits (NOT just the latest commit, but ALL commits that will be included in the pull request!!!), and draft a pull request summary 3. You have the capability to call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested, batch your tool calls together for optimal performance. ALWAYS run the following commands in parallel: - Create new branch if needed - Push to remote with -u flag if needed - Create PR using gh pr create with the format below. Use a HEREDOC to pass the body to ensure correct formatting. gh pr create --title "the pr title" --body "$(cat <<'EOF' ## Summary <1-3 bullet points> ## Test plan [Checklist of TODOs for testing the pull request...] 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) EOF )" Important: - NEVER update the git config - DO NOT use the TodoWrite or Task tools - Return the PR URL when you're done, so the user can see it # Other common operations - View comments on a Github PR: gh api repos/foo/bar/pulls/123/comments", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"command": {"type": "string", "description": "The command to execute"}, "timeout": {"type": "number", "description": "Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000)"}, "description": {"type": "string", "description": "Clear, concise description of what this command does in 5-10 words, in active voice. This helps you track progress, organize complex tasks, and demonstrate thoroughness to the user. It also helps the user understand the progress of the task and overall progress of their requests. ## When to Use This Tool Use this tool proactively in these scenarios: 1. Complex multi-step tasks - When a task requires 3 or more distinct steps or actions 2. Non-trivial and complex tasks - Tasks that require careful planning or multiple operations 3. User explicitly requests todo list - When the user directly asks you to use the todo list 4. User provides multiple tasks - When users provide a list of things to be done (numbered or comma-separated) 5. After receiving new instructions - Immediately capture user requirements as todos 6. When you start working on a task - Mark it as in_progress BEFORE beginning work. Ideally you should only have one todo as in_progress at a time 7. After completing a task - Mark it as completed and add any new follow-up tasks discovered during implementation ## When NOT to Use This Tool Skip using this tool when: 1. There is only a single, straightforward task 2. The task is trivial and tracking it provides no organizational benefit 3. The task can be completed in less than 3 trivial steps 4. The task is purely conversational or informational NOTE that you should not use this tool if there is only one trivial task to do. In this case you are better off just doing the task directly. ## Examples of When to Use the Todo List User: I want to add a dark mode toggle to the application settings. Make sure you run the tests and build when you're done! Assistant: I'll help add a dark mode toggle to your application settings. Let me create a todo list to track this implementation. *Creates todo list with the following items:* 1. Creating dark mode toggle component in Settings page 2. Adding dark mode state management (context/store) 3. Implementing CSS-in-JS styles for dark theme 4. Updating existing components to support theme switching 5. Running tests and build process, addressing any failures or errors that occur *Begins working on the first task* The assistant used the todo list because: 1. Adding dark mode is a multi-step feature requiring UI, state management, and styling changes 2. The user explicitly requested tests and build be run afterward 3. The assistant inferred that tests and build need to pass by adding "Ensure tests and build succeed" as the final task User: Help me rename the function getCwd to getCurrentWorkingDirectory across my project Assistant: Let me first search through your codebase to find all occurrences of 'getCwd'. *Uses grep or search tools to locate all instances of getCwd in the codebase* Assistant: I've found 15 instances of 'getCwd' across 8 different files. Let me create a todo list to track these changes. *Creates todo list with specific items for each file that needs updating* The assistant used the todo list because: 1. First, the assistant searched to understand the scope of the task 2. Upon finding multiple occurrences across different files, it determined this was a complex task with multiple steps 3. The todo list helps ensure every instance is tracked and updated systematically 4. Contents of /home/adrien/Documents/pd/stock-correlation/CLAUDE.md (project instructions, checked into the codebase): # CLAUDE.md This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository. ## Project Overview This is a comprehensive Market Leadership Network Analysis and Backtesting project that identifies leadership relationships between stocks using Granger causality analysis and tests trading strategies based on these relationships. The project analyzes time-series stock data to build directed networks showing which stocks lead others in price movements, then applies these insights through a sophisticated backtesting framework. ## Architecture The project follows a modular architecture with two main systems: ### 1. Network Analysis System - **Data Loading** (`src/data/data_loader.py`): Handles downloading, caching, and preprocessing stock data from Yahoo Finance - **Network Construction** (`src/network/network_builder.py`): Builds leadership networks using Granger causality tests - **Leadership Analysis** (`src/analysis/leadership_analyzer.py`): Analyzes networks to identify market leaders and followers ### 2. Backtesting System (`src/backtesting/`) - **Backtest Engine** (`backtest_engine.py`): Core backtesting framework with portfolio management - **Strategies** (`strategies/`): Leadership-following, mean reversion, and pairs trading strategies - **Portfolio Management** (`portfolio/`): Portfolio construction and risk management - **Performance Metrics** (`metrics/`): Performance evaluation and analytics ### Key Classes - `DataLoader`: Manages data retrieval, caching, and market-adjustment calculations - `NetworkBuilder`: Performs Granger causality tests and constructs directed networks - `LeadershipAnalyzer`: Calculates centrality measures and ranks market leaders - `BacktestEngine`: Core backtesting framework with trade execution and portfolio tracking - `LeadershipStrategy`: Implements leadership-following trading strategies - `PortfolioManager`: Handles portfolio construction and position management - `RiskManager`: Implements risk controls and position sizing - `PerformanceMetrics`: Calculates comprehensive performance analytics ## Common Commands ### Network Analysis ```bash # Run complete analysis with default config python src/main.py # Run with custom config python src/main.py --config config/config.yaml # Force data refresh python src/main.py --force-refresh # Specify output directory python src/main.py --output-dir custom_results/ ``` ### Backtesting ```bash # Run backtest with default configuration python run_backtest.py # Run backtest with custom config python run_backtest.py --config config/backtest_config.yaml # Debug backtest execution python debug_backtest.py # Test individual strategies python debug_strategy.py ``` ### Parameter Optimization ```bash # Optimize leadership thresholds python scripts/optimize_thresholds.py # Run unified workflow (analysis + backtest) python scripts/unified_workflow.py ``` ### Environment Setup ```bash # Create virtual environment (recommended) python -m venv venv source venv/bin/activate # On Windows: venv\Scripts\activate # Install dependencies pip install -r requirements.txt ``` ## Configuration The project uses YAML configuration files: ### Network Analysis (`config/config.yaml`) - **Data Source**: Yahoo Finance with Vietnamese stock tickers (VIC.VN, VCB.VN, etc.) - **Analysis Parameters**: Granger causality settings (max lag: 5, p-value threshold: 0.02) - **Time Period**: Configurable date range (2020-01-01 to 2025-09-23) - **Market Adjustment**: Optional OLS regression for market-adjusted returns (default: false) - **Output Settings**: Controls visualization and data saving options ### Backtesting (`config/backtest_config.yaml`) - **Portfolio Parameters**: Initial capital ($1M), position sizing, risk limits - **Strategy Settings**: Leadership thresholds, maximum positions, holding periods - **Risk Management**: Max drawdown (15%), beta limits, correlation constraints - **Output Configuration**: Plotting, reporting, and trade logging settings ## Data Flow ### Network Analysis Pipeline 1. **Data Loading**: Downloads stock prices, calculates returns, performs market adjustment 2. **Network Building**: Tests all stock pairs for Granger causality relationships 3. **Leadership Analysis**: Calculates centrality measures and identifies leaders/followers 4. **Output Generation**: Saves rankings, network visualizations, and analysis results ### Backtesting Pipeline 1. **Strategy Application**: Applies leadership-following, mean reversion, and pairs trading strategies 2. **Portfolio Management**: Handles position sizing, risk management, and rebalancing 3. **Performance Evaluation**: Calculates metrics, generates reports, and creates visualizations 4. **Optimization**: Automates parameter tuning for improved strategy performance ## Key Features ### Network Analysis - **Market Adjustment**: Uses OLS regression to calculate market-adjusted returns - **Caching**: Implements data caching to avoid repeated downloads - **Multiple Centrality Measures**: Out-degree, PageRank, betweenness, closeness, eigenvector - **Composite Leadership Scoring**: Weighted combination of centrality measures - **Network Visualization**: Configurable network graphs with leadership scores ### Backtesting System - **Multi-Strategy Framework**: Leadership-following, mean reversion, and pairs trading strategies - **Risk Management**: Position sizing, drawdown limits, correlation constraints - **Portfolio Optimization**: Dynamic rebalancing and performance monitoring - **Performance Analytics**: Comprehensive metrics and visualization - **Parameter Optimization**: Automated hyperparameter tuning with Optuna ### Market Focus - **Vietnamese Stock Market**: Optimized for Vietnamese stocks (VIC.VN, VCB.VN, etc.) - **Yahoo Finance Integration**: Real-time data downloading and caching - **Benchmark Integration**: VNINDEX benchmark for market adjustment ## Output Files ### Network Analysis Results - `leadership_ranking.csv`: Ranked list of market leaders - `centrality_measures.csv`: All centrality measures for each stock - `significant_edges.csv`: List of significant leadership relationships - `leadership_hierarchy.json`: Hierarchical analysis results - `leadership_network.png`: Network visualization ### Backtesting Results - `backtest_results/`: Contains all backtest outputs - `portfolio_history.csv`: Daily portfolio values and positions - `trades.csv`: Detailed trade log with entries and exits - `performance_metrics.csv`: Comprehensive performance analytics - `plots/`: Performance charts and visualizations - `reports/`: Detailed backtest reports ### Optimization Results - `optimization_results/`: Parameter optimization outputs - `best_params.json`: Optimal parameters found - `optimization_history.csv`: Complete optimization trials - `performance_summary.csv`: Performance across parameter space ## Testing No formal test suite exists. Debug and validate using: - `debug_return.py`: Return calculation debugging utilities - Manual validation through script execution and output analysis ## Dependencies Key libraries: pandas>=1.5.0, numpy>=1.21.0, yfinance>=0.2.0, statsmodels, networkx>=2.8.0, matplotlib>=3.5.0, seaborn>=0.11.0, scikit-learn>=1.5.0, optuna>=4.0.0, plotly>=6.0.0, PyYAML, community, joblib>=1.2.0, kaleido>=1.0.0 ## Notes - The project assumes stationary time series (ADF test configurable) - Network edges represent Granger causality relationships (A → B means A leads B) - Leadership scores are composite measures emphasizing out-degree centrality - Backtesting includes realistic constraints: transaction costs, slippage, and risk limits - Vietnamese market focus with VNINDEX as primary benchmark - No formal linting or type checking configured - code quality maintained through manual review - Data caching implemented to avoid repeated Yahoo Finance downloads - All results excluded from version control (see .gitignore) # important-instruction-reminders Do what has been asked; nothing more, nothing less. **Controllers**: API endpoints under `app/controllers/api/v1/` - **Services**: Business logic in `app/services/` organized by domain (connections, connectors, syncs, ETL, AI) - **Temporal Workflows**: Orchestration logic in `app/services/temporal/workflows/` - **Temporal Activities**: Individual workflow steps in `app/services/temporal/activities/` - **Models**: ActiveRecord models representing core entities (Connection, Connector, Sync, Chat, etc.) ### Key Services 1. **ETL Pipeline**: Handles data extraction from sources, transformation, and loading to DuckDB - `Ai::ChatMetadataGeneratorServiceV2`: DSPy-based chat metadata generation - `Ai::QueryRefactoringService`: Query optimization and refactoring 3. **Connection Management**: Handles source/destination connections - `ConnectionDataSyncWorkflow`: Main sync orchestration - `SyncWorkflow`: Individual sync execution - `DataAgentWorkflow`: Chat processing pipeline - Activities handle atomic operations like API calls, database writes ## Testing Approach -    505→    def _calculate_entity_similarity(self, analysis1: Dict, analysis2: Dict) -> float:
   506→        """计算两个实体的相似度"""
   507→        # 基于维度得分的相似度
   508→        scores1 = analysis1.get('dimension_scores', {})
   509→        scores2 = analysis2.get('dimension_scores', {})

   512→            return 0.0
   513→        
   514→        # 计算余弦相似度
   515→        common_dims = set(scores1.keys()) & set(scores2.keys())
   516→        if not common_dims:
   517→            return 0.0
   518→        
   519→        dot_product = sum(scores1[dim] * scores2[dim] for dim in common_dims)
   520→        magnitude1 = sum(score ** 2 for score in scores1.values()) ** 0.5
   521→        magnitude2 = sum(score ** 2 for score in scores2.values()) ** 0.5
   522→        
   523→        if magnitude1 == 0 or magnitude2 == 0:
   524→            return 0.0
   525→

         """基础概念搜索 - 简单直接"""
         
         def __init__(self, knowledge_graph_manager):
             self.kg_manager = knowledge_graph_manager
         
         async def find_companies_by_concept(self, concept_name: str) -> List[Dict]:
             """根据概念查找相关公司"""
             # Input validation following existing exception patterns
             if not concept_name or not isinstance(concept_name, str):
                 raise ValidationError("概念名称不能为空", field="concept_name", value=concept_name)
             
             # Simple graph operations with clear error handling
             graph_file = self.kg_manager.get_latest_graph_file()
             if not graph_file:
                 logger.warning("没有找到知识图谱文件")
                 return []
                 
             graph, _ = await self.kg_manager.storage_manager.load_graph(graph_file)
             if not graph:
                 logger.warning("加载知识图谱失败")
                 return []
             
             # Direct graph traversal
             concept_node = None
             for node_id, node_data in graph.nodes(data=True):
                 if (node_data.get('type') == 'concept' and 
                     node_data.get('name') == concept_name):
                     concept_node = node_id
                     break
             
             # Simple relationship extraction
             related_companies = []
             for successor in graph.successors(concept_node):
                 node_data = graph.nodes[successor]
                 if node_data.get('type') == 'company':
                     edge_data = graph.get_edge_data(concept_node, successor)
                     company_info = {
                         'name': node_data.get('name', ''),
                         'stock_code': node_data.get('stock_code', ''),
                         'industry': node_data.get('industry', ''),
                         'relation_strength': edge_data.get('weight', 1.0),
                         'confidence': edge_data.get('confidence', 'medium')
                     }
                     related_companies.append(company_info)
             
             return sorted(related_companies, 
                          key=lambda x: x['relation_strength'], reverse=True)

        Args:

            limit: 返回结果数量限制

            # 搜索内容节点

            for node_id, node_data in graph.nodes(data=True):

                    )

                            'content_id': node_id,
                            'content_hash': node_data.get('content_hash', ''),
                            'content_type': node_data.get('content_type', ''),
                            'file_path': node_data.get('file_path', ''),

                            'match_score': match_score,

        """

        if entity_type and entity_type not in ['company', 'industry', 'concept', 'dimension']:
            raise ValidationError("无效的实体类型", field="entity_type", value=entity_type)
        
        try:

            graph_file = self.kg_manager.get_latest_graph_file()
            if not graph_file:

            graph, _ = await self.kg_manager.storage_manager.load_graph(graph_file)

            entity_nodes = []
            for node_id, node_data in graph.nodes(data=True):

            if not entity_nodes:
                logger.info(f"未找到实体: {entity_name}")
                return []
            
            # 查找相关内容
            content_results = []
            for entity_node in entity_nodes:
                # 查找直接连接的内容节点
                for successor in graph.successors(entity_node):
                    node_data = graph.nodes[successor]
                    if node_data.get('type') == 'content':
                        edge_data = graph.get_edge_data(entity_node, successor)
                        content_info = {
                            'content_id': successor,
                            'content_hash': node_data.get('content_hash', ''),

                            'created_at': node_data.get('created_at', ''),
                            'entity_relation': 'direct'
                        }
                        content_results.append(content_info)
                
                # 查找通过其他实体连接的内容节点（2跳）
                for neighbor in graph.predecessors(entity_node):

        """
        # 输入验证

        if len(keywords) == 0:

        for keyword in keywords:

                return []
            
            # 搜索内容节点
            results = []
            keywords_lower = [kw.strip().lower() for kw in keywords]
            
            for node_id, node_data in graph.nodes(data=True):
                if node_data.get('type') == 'content':
                    full_content = node_data.get('full_content', '')
                    content_summary = node_data.get('content_summary', '')
                    
                    # 检查关键词匹配
                    match_result = self._calculate_keyword_match(
                        keywords_lower, full_content, content_summary, require_all
                    )
                    
                    if match_result['matches'] > 0:
                        result = {

                            'content_hash': node_data.get('content_hash', ''),
                            'content_type': node_data.get('content_type', ''),
                            'file_path': node_data.get('file_path', ''),

    def _calculate_content_match(self, query: str, query_lower: str, 
                                full_content: str, content_summary: str) -> float:
        """计算内容匹配分数"""
        score = 0.0
        
        # 在完整内容中搜索
        if full_content:
            # 完全匹配
            if query in full_content:
                score += 10.0
            
            # 大小写不敏感匹配
            if query_lower in full_content.lower():
                score += 8.0
            
            # 部分匹配
            if len(query) > 3:
                words = query_lower.split()
                matched_words = sum(1 for word in words if word in full_content.lower())
                score += matched_words * 2.0
            
            # 正则表达式匹配（更灵活的搜索）
            try:
                pattern = re.compile(query, re.IGNORECASE)
                matches = pattern.findall(full_content)
                score += len(matches) * 3.0
            except re.error:
                pass  # 忽略无效的正则表达式
        
        # 在摘要中搜索（分数较低）
        if content_summary:
            if query in content_summary:
                score += 5.0
            if query_lower in content_summary.lower():
                score += 3.0
        
        return score
    
    def _calculate_keyword_match(self, keywords_lower: List[str], full_content: str, 
                               content_summary: str, require_all: bool) -> Dict:
        """计算关键词匹配结果"""
        content_lower = full_content.lower()
        summary_lower = content_summary.lower()
        
        matched_keywords = []
        matches = 0
        
        for keyword in keywords_lower:
            keyword_found = False
            
            # 在完整内容中查找
            if keyword in content_lower:
                matched_keywords.append(keyword)
                matches += 1
                keyword_found = True
            
            # 在摘要中查找（分数较低）
            elif keyword in summary_lower:
                matched_keywords.append(keyword)
                matches += 0.5
                keyword_found = True
            
            # 如果要求所有关键词都匹配，有一个没找到就返回
            if require_all and not keyword_found:
                return {
                    'matches': 0,
                    'score': 0.0,
                    'matched_keywords': []
                }
        
        # 计算分数
        if require_all:
            score = matches * 10.0  # 所有关键词都匹配，高分
        else:
            score = matches * 2.0  # 任意关键词匹配
        
        return {
            'matches': matches,
            'score': score,
            'matched_keywords': matched_keywords
        }

        """获取与内容相关的实体"""
        related_entities = []

            edge_data = graph.get_edge_data(predecessor, content_id)
            node_data = graph.nodes[predecessor]
            
            entity_info = {
                'entity_id': predecessor,
                'name': node_data.get('name', ''),
                'type': node_data.get('type', ''),
                'relation_strength': edge_data.get('weight', 1.0),
                'relation_type': edge_data.get('relation_type', 'mentions')
            }
            related_entities.append(entity_info)

Contents of /Users/karthiksivadas/Development/polymetrics/CLAUDE.md (project instructions, checked into the codebase): # CLAUDE.md This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository. ## Project Overview Polymetrics is an open-source tool for multi-source data extraction, visualization, and analytics. The project consists of: - A Rails API backend (`platform/`) - A React/TypeScript frontend (`ui/`) - Ruby-based data connectors (`ruby_connectors/`) - Temporal workflow orchestration for ETL processes ## Development Commands ### Backend (Rails API) ```bash # From the platform/ directory bundle install # Install Ruby dependencies rails db:create # Create database rails db:migrate # Run migrations rails db:seed # Seed initial data rails server # Start Rails server on port 3000 rails console # Start Rails console # Testing bundle exec rspec # Run all tests bundle exec rspec spec/path/to/spec.rb # Run specific test file # Linting bundle exec rubocop # Run RuboCop linter bundle exec rubocop -a # Auto-fix linting issues ``` ### Frontend (React/TypeScript) ```bash # From the ui/ directory bun install # Install dependencies bun run dev # Start development server bun run build # Build for production bun run test # Run tests bun run coverage # Run tests with coverage bun run lint # Run ESLint bun run pretty # Format code with Prettier ``` ### Ruby Connectors ```bash # From the ruby_connectors/ directory bundle install # Install dependencies bundle exec rspec # Run tests bundle exec rubocop # Run linter ``` ### Docker Development ```bash # From the root directory docker-compose up -d # Start all services (PostgreSQL, DragonflyDB, Temporal, Rails, UI) docker-compose down # Stop all services docker-compose logs -f [service] # View logs docker-compose exec rails bundle exec rails console # Rails console # Production deployment docker-compose -f docker-compose.production.yml up -d ``` ### Temporal Workers ```bash # Rails Temporal worker bundle exec rails temporal:worker # Ruby connectors Temporal worker bundle exec ruby_connectors temporal_worker ``` ## Architecture Overview ### Backend Structure The Rails API follows a service-oriented architecture: - **Controllers**: API endpoints under `app/controllers/api/v1/` - **Services**: Business logic in `app/services/` organized by domain (connections, connectors, syncs, ETL, AI) - **Temporal Workflows**: Orchestration logic in `app/services/temporal/workflows/` - **Temporal Activities**: Individual workflow steps in `app/services/temporal/activities/` - **Models**: ActiveRecord models representing core entities (Connection, Connector, Sync, Chat, etc.) ### Key Services 1. **ETL Pipeline**: Handles data extraction from sources, transformation, and loading to DuckDB - Extractors handle API and database sources - Uses Temporal workflows for orchestration - Implements incremental sync with deduplication 2. **AI/Data Agent**: Chat-based interface for data queries - Uses DSPy.rb for structured AI programming (migrating from LangChain) - Generates SQL queries from natural language - Creates summaries and visualizations - Includes intelligent connector selection service - Key services: - `Ai::Etl::ConnectorSelectionServiceV2`: DSPy-based connector selection - `Ai::ChatMetadataGeneratorServiceV2`: DSPy-based chat metadata generation - `Ai::QueryRefactoringService`: Query optimization and refactoring 3. **Connection Management**: Handles source/destination connections - Supports multiple connector types (GitHub, Salesforce, DuckDB, PostgreSQL) - Schema discovery and mapping ### Frontend Architecture - Built with React + TypeScript + Vite - Uses TanStack Router for routing - TanStack Query for API state management - Tailwind CSS + shadcn/ui for styling - JSON Schema Forms for dynamic connector configuration ### Temporal Workflows The system uses Temporal for reliable distributed workflow execution: - `ConnectionDataSyncWorkflow`: Main sync orchestration - `SyncWorkflow`: Individual sync execution - `DataAgentWorkflow`: Chat processing pipeline - Activities handle atomic operations like API calls, database writes ## Testing Approach - RSpec for Rails API tests with VCR for external API mocking - Vitest for React component and unit tests - Factory Bot for test data generation - Database Cleaner for test isolation ## Environment Variables Key environment variables include: - `TEMPORAL_HOST`, `TEMPORAL_PORT`, `TEMPORAL_NAMESPACE`: Temporal configuration - `DATABASE_URL`: PostgreSQL connection - `REDIS_URL`: DragonflyDB connection (Redis-compatible) - `OPENAI_API_KEY` or `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`: LLM provider credentials - `GITHUB_ACCESS_TOKEN`: For GitHub connector authentication - `SECRET_KEY_BASE`: Rails secret key (required for production) ## DSPy Framework Integration The project is migrating from LangChain to DSPy.rb for structured AI programming: ### DSPy Architecture - **Signatures**: Type-safe input/output definitions using T::Struct and enums - **Modular Services**: Component-based architecture with clear separation of concerns - **Error Handling**: Centralized error management with structured responses - **Type Safety**: Strong typing with Sorbet for better code maintainability ### DSPy Services 1. **ConnectorSelectionServiceV2**: Intelligent ETL connector selection - Analyzes user requirements and recommends optimal connectors - Handles pipeline creation and clarification messages - Components: ConnectorFormatter, PipelineActionHandler, MessageHandler, ErrorHandler 2. **ChatMetadataGeneratorServiceV2**: Enhanced chat processing - Generates comprehensive metadata for chat sessions - Supports complex conversation context and error recovery 3. **QueryRefactoringService**: SQL query optimization - Refactors natural language queries for better execution - Handles complex query patterns and optimization ## Code Style - Ruby: Follow RuboCop configuration (double quotes, frozen string literals) - TypeScript: ESLint + Prettier configuration - Commit messages should be descriptive and follow conventional format - When ever we create a new file named as *.rb file always remember to add *.rb.md explaing the code in detail - Always write the code which is modular, readable, writeable and maintainable - Always Update claude.md when we update the code in a major way # important-instruction-reminders Do what has been asked; nothing more, nothing less. Contents of /home/adrien/Documents/pd/stock-correlation/CLAUDE.md (project instructions, checked into the codebase): # CLAUDE.md This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository. ## Project Overview This is a comprehensive Market Leadership Network Analysis and Backtesting project that identifies leadership relationships between stocks using Granger causality analysis and tests trading strategies based on these relationships. The project analyzes time-series stock data to build directed networks showing which stocks lead others in price movements, then applies these insights through a sophisticated backtesting framework. ## Architecture The project follows a modular architecture with two main systems: ### 1. Network Analysis System - **Data Loading** (`src/data/data_loader.py`): Handles downloading, caching, and preprocessing stock data from Yahoo Finance - **Network Construction** (`src/network/network_builder.py`): Builds leadership networks using Granger causality tests - **Leadership Analysis** (`src/analysis/leadership_analyzer.py`): Analyzes networks to identify market leaders and followers ### 2. Backtesting System (`src/backtesting/`) - **Backtest Engine** (`backtest_engine.py`): Core backtesting framework with portfolio management - **Strategies** (`strategies/`): Leadership-following, mean reversion, and pairs trading strategies - **Portfolio Management** (`portfolio/`): Portfolio construction and risk management - **Performance Metrics** (`metrics/`): Performance evaluation and analytics ### Key Classes - `DataLoader`: Manages data retrieval, caching, and market-adjustment calculations - `NetworkBuilder`: Performs Granger causality tests and constructs directed networks - `LeadershipAnalyzer`: Calculates centrality measures and ranks market leaders - `BacktestEngine`: Core backtesting framework with trade execution and portfolio tracking - `LeadershipStrategy`: Implements leadership-following trading strategies - `PortfolioManager`: Handles portfolio construction and position management - `RiskManager`: Implements risk controls and position sizing - `PerformanceMetrics`: Calculates comprehensive performance analytics ## Common Commands ### Network Analysis ```bash # Run complete analysis with default config python src/main.py # Run with custom config python src/main.py --config config/config.yaml # Force data refresh python src/main.py --force-refresh # Specify output directory python src/main.py --output-dir custom_results/ ``` ### Backtesting ```bash # Run backtest with default configuration python run_backtest.py # Run backtest with custom config python run_backtest.py --config config/backtest_config.yaml # Debug backtest execution python debug_backtest.py # Test individual strategies python debug_strategy.py ``` ### Parameter Optimization ```bash # Optimize leadership thresholds python scripts/optimize_thresholds.py # Run unified workflow (analysis + backtest) python scripts/unified_workflow.py ``` ### Environment Setup ```bash # Create virtual environment (recommended) python -m venv venv source venv/bin/activate # On Windows: venv\Scripts\activate # Install dependencies pip install -r requirements.txt ``` ## Configuration The project uses YAML configuration files: ### Network Analysis (`config/config.yaml`) - **Data Source**: Yahoo Finance with Vietnamese stock tickers (VIC.VN, VCB.VN, etc.) - **Analysis Parameters**: Granger causality settings (max lag: 5, p-value threshold: 0.02) - **Time Period**: Configurable date range (2020-01-01 to 2025-09-23) - **Market Adjustment**: Optional OLS regression for market-adjusted returns (default: false) - **Output Settings**: Controls visualization and data saving options ### Backtesting (`config/backtest_config.yaml`) - **Portfolio Parameters**: Initial capital ($1M), position sizing, risk limits - **Strategy Settings**: Leadership thresholds, maximum positions, holding periods - **Risk Management**: Max drawdown (15%), beta limits, correlation constraints - **Output Configuration**: Plotting, reporting, and trade logging settings ## Data Flow ### Network Analysis Pipeline 1. **Data Loading**: Downloads stock prices, calculates returns, performs market adjustment 2. **Network Building**: Tests all stock pairs for Granger causality relationships 3. **Leadership Analysis**: Calculates centrality measures and identifies leaders/followers 4. **Output Generation**: Saves rankings, network visualizations, and analysis results ### Backtesting Pipeline 1. **Strategy Application**: Applies leadership-following, mean reversion, and pairs trading strategies 2. **Portfolio Management**: Handles position sizing, risk management, and rebalancing 3. **Performance Evaluation**: Calculates metrics, generates reports, and creates visualizations 4. **Optimization**: Automates parameter tuning for improved strategy performance ## Key Features ### Network Analysis - **Market Adjustment**: Uses OLS regression to calculate market-adjusted returns - **Caching**: Implements data caching to avoid repeated downloads - **Multiple Centrality Measures**: Out-degree, PageRank, betweenness, closeness, eigenvector - **Composite Leadership Scoring**: Weighted combination of centrality measures - **Network Visualization**: Configurable network graphs with leadership scores ### Backtesting System - **Multi-Strategy Framework**: Leadership-following, mean reversion, and pairs trading strategies - **Risk Management**: Position sizing, drawdown limits, correlation constraints - **Portfolio Optimization**: Dynamic rebalancing and performance monitoring - **Performance Analytics**: Comprehensive metrics and visualization - **Parameter Optimization**: Automated hyperparameter tuning with Optuna ### Market Focus - **Vietnamese Stock Market**: Optimized for Vietnamese stocks (VIC.VN, VCB.VN, etc.) - **Yahoo Finance Integration**: Real-time data downloading and caching - **Benchmark Integration**: VNINDEX benchmark for market adjustment ## Output Files ### Network Analysis Results - `leadership_ranking.csv`: Ranked list of market leaders - `centrality_measures.csv`: All centrality measures for each stock - `significant_edges.csv`: List of significant leadership relationships - `leadership_hierarchy.json`: Hierarchical analysis results - `leadership_network.png`: Network visualization ### Backtesting Results - `backtest_results/`: Contains all backtest outputs - `portfolio_history.csv`: Daily portfolio values and positions - `trades.csv`: Detailed trade log with entries and exits - `performance_metrics.csv`: Comprehensive performance analytics - `plots/`: Performance charts and visualizations - `reports/`: Detailed backtest reports ### Optimization Results - `optimization_results/`: Parameter optimization outputs - `best_params.json`: Optimal parameters found - `optimization_history.csv`: Complete optimization trials - `performance_summary.csv`: Performance across parameter space ## Testing No formal test suite exists. Debug and validate using: - `debug_return.py`: Return calculation debugging utilities - Manual validation through script execution and output analysis ## Dependencies Key libraries: pandas>=1.5.0, numpy>=1.21.0, yfinance>=0.2.0, statsmodels, networkx>=2.8.0, matplotlib>=3.5.0, seaborn>=0.11.0, scikit-learn>=1.5.0, optuna>=4.0.0, plotly>=6.0.0, PyYAML, community, joblib>=1.2.0, kaleido>=1.0.0 ## Notes - The project assumes stationary time series (ADF test configurable) - Network edges represent Granger causality relationships (A → B means A leads B) - Leadership scores are composite measures emphasizing out-degree centrality - Backtesting includes realistic constraints: transaction costs, slippage, and risk limits - Vietnamese market focus with VNINDEX as primary benchmark - No formal linting or type checking configured - code quality maintained through manual review - Data caching implemented to avoid repeated Yahoo Finance downloads - All results excluded from version control (see .gitignore) # important-instruction-reminders Do what has been asked; nothing more, nothing less. The project consists of: - A Rails API backend (`platform/`) - A React/TypeScript frontend (`ui/`) - Ruby-based data connectors (`ruby_connectors/`) - Temporal workflow orchestration for ETL processes ## Development Commands ### Backend (Rails API) ```bash # From the platform/ directory bundle install # Install Ruby dependencies rails db:create # Create database rails db:migrate # Run migrations rails db:seed # Seed initial data rails server # Start Rails server on port 3000 rails console # Start Rails console # Testing bundle exec rspec # Run all tests bundle exec rspec spec/path/to/spec.rb # Run specific test file # Linting bundle exec rubocop # Run RuboCop linter bundle exec rubocop -a # Auto-fix linting issues ``` ### Frontend (React/TypeScript) ```bash # From the ui/ directory bun install # Install dependencies bun run dev # Start development server bun run build # Build for production bun run test # Run tests bun run coverage # Run tests with coverage bun run lint # Run ESLint bun run pretty # Format code with Prettier ``` ### Ruby Connectors ```bash # From the ruby_connectors/ directory bundle install # Install dependencies bundle exec rspec # Run tests bundle exec rubocop # Run linter ``` ### Docker Development ```bash # From the root directory docker-compose up -d # Start all services (PostgreSQL, DragonflyDB, Temporal, Rails, UI) docker-compose down # Stop all services docker-compose logs -f [service] # View logs docker-compose exec rails bundle exec rails console # Rails console # Production deployment docker-compose -f docker-compose.production.yml up -d ``` ### Temporal Workers ```bash # Rails Temporal worker bundle exec rails temporal:worker # Ruby connectors Temporal worker bundle exec ruby_connectors temporal_worker ``` ## Architecture Overview ### Backend Structure The Rails API follows a service-oriented architecture: - **Controllers**: API endpoints under `app/controllers/api/v1/` - **Services**: Business logic in `app/services/` organized by domain (connections, connectors, syncs, ETL, AI) - **Temporal Workflows**: Orchestration logic in `app/services/temporal/workflows/` - **Temporal Activities**: Individual workflow steps in `app/services/temporal/activities/` - **Models**: ActiveRecord models representing core entities (Connection, Connector, Sync, Chat, etc.) ### Key Services 1. **ETL Pipeline**: Handles data extraction from sources, transformation, and loading to DuckDB - Extractors handle API and database sources - Uses Temporal workflows for orchestration - Implements incremental sync with deduplication 2. **AI/Data Agent**: Chat-based interface for data queries - Uses DSPy.rb for structured AI programming (migrating from LangChain) - Generates SQL queries from natural language - Creates summaries and visualizations - Includes intelligent connector selection service - Key services: - `Ai::Etl::ConnectorSelectionServiceV2`: DSPy-based connector selection - `Ai::ChatMetadataGeneratorServiceV2`: DSPy-based chat metadata generation - `Ai::QueryRefactoringService`: Query optimization and refactoring 3. **Connection Management**: Handles source/destination connections - Supports multiple connector types (GitHub, Salesforce, DuckDB, PostgreSQL) - Schema discovery and mapping ### Frontend Architecture - Built with React + TypeScript + Vite - Uses TanStack Router for routing - TanStack Query for API state management - Tailwind CSS + shadcn/ui for styling - JSON Schema Forms for dynamic connector configuration ### Temporal Workflows The system uses Temporal for reliable distributed workflow execution: - `ConnectionDataSyncWorkflow`: Main sync orchestration - `SyncWorkflow`: Individual sync execution - `DataAgentWorkflow`: Chat processing pipeline - Activities handle atomic operations like API calls, database writes ## Testing Approach - RSpec for Rails API tests with VCR for external API mocking - Vitest for React component and unit tests - Factory Bot for test data generation - Database Cleaner for test isolation ## Environment Variables Key environment variables include: - `TEMPORAL_HOST`, `TEMPORAL_PORT`, `TEMPORAL_NAMESPACE`: Temporal configuration - `DATABASE_URL`: PostgreSQL connection - `REDIS_URL`: DragonflyDB connection (Redis-compatible) - `OPENAI_API_KEY` or `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`: LLM provider credentials - `GITHUB_ACCESS_TOKEN`: For GitHub connector authentication - `SECRET_KEY_BASE`: Rails secret key (required for production) ## DSPy Framework Integration The project is migrating from LangChain to DSPy.rb for structured AI programming: ### DSPy Architecture - **Signatures**: Type-safe input/output definitions using T::Struct and enums - **Modular Services**: Component-based architecture with clear separation of concerns - **Error Handling**: Centralized error management with structured responses - **Type Safety**: Strong typing with Sorbet for better code maintainability ### DSPy Services 1. **ConnectorSelectionServiceV2**: Intelligent ETL connector selection - Analyzes user requirements and recommends optimal connectors - Handles pipeline creation and clarification messages - Components: ConnectorFormatter, PipelineActionHandler, MessageHandler, ErrorHandler 2. **ChatMetadataGeneratorServiceV2**: Enhanced chat processing - Generates comprehensive metadata for chat sessions - Supports complex conversation context and error recovery 3. **QueryRefactoringService**: SQL query optimization - Refactors natural language queries for better execution - Handles complex query patterns and optimization ## Code Style - Ruby: Follow RuboCop configuration (double quotes, frozen string literals) - TypeScript: ESLint + Prettier configuration - Commit messages should be descriptive and follow conventional format - The project consists of: - A Rails API backend (`platform/`) - A React/TypeScript frontend (`ui/`) - Ruby-based data connectors (`ruby_connectors/`) - Temporal workflow orchestration for ETL processes ## Development Commands ### Backend (Rails API) ```bash # From the platform/ directory bundle install # Install Ruby dependencies rails db:create # Create database rails db:migrate # Run migrations rails db:seed # Seed initial data rails server # Start Rails server on port 3000 rails console # Start Rails console # Testing bundle exec rspec # Run all tests bundle exec rspec spec/path/to/spec.rb # Run specific test file # Linting bundle exec rubocop # Run RuboCop linter bundle exec rubocop -a # Auto-fix linting issues ``` ### Frontend (React/TypeScript) ```bash # From the ui/ directory bun install # Install dependencies bun run dev # Start development server bun run build # Build for production bun run test # Run tests bun run coverage # Run tests with coverage bun run lint # Run ESLint bun run pretty # Format code with Prettier ``` ### Ruby Connectors ```bash # From the ruby_connectors/ directory bundle install # Install dependencies bundle exec rspec # Run tests bundle exec rubocop # Run linter ``` ### Docker Development ```bash # From the root directory docker-compose up -d # Start all services (PostgreSQL, DragonflyDB, Temporal, Rails, UI) docker-compose down # Stop all services docker-compose logs -f [service] # View logs docker-compose exec rails bundle exec rails console # Rails console # Production deployment docker-compose -f docker-compose.production.yml up -d ``` ### Temporal Workers ```bash # Rails Temporal worker bundle exec rails temporal:worker # Ruby connectors Temporal worker bundle exec ruby_connectors temporal_worker ``` ## Architecture Overview ### Backend Structure The Rails API follows a service-oriented architecture: - **Controllers**: API endpoints under `app/controllers/api/v1/` - **Services**: Business logic in `app/services/` organized by domain (connections, connectors, syncs, ETL, AI) - **Temporal Workflows**: Orchestration logic in `app/services/temporal/workflows/` - **Temporal Activities**: Individual workflow steps in `app/services/temporal/activities/` - **Models**: ActiveRecord models representing core entities (Connection, Connector, Sync, Chat, etc.) ### Key Services 1. **ETL Pipeline**: Handles data extraction from sources, transformation, and loading to DuckDB - Extractors handle API and database sources - Uses Temporal workflows for orchestration - Implements incremental sync with deduplication 2. **AI/Data Agent**: Chat-based interface for data queries - Uses DSPy.rb for structured AI programming (migrating from LangChain) - Generates SQL queries from natural language - Creates summaries and visualizations - Includes intelligent connector selection service - Key services: - `Ai::Etl::ConnectorSelectionServiceV2`: DSPy-based connector selection - `Ai::ChatMetadataGeneratorServiceV2`: DSPy-based chat metadata generation - `Ai::QueryRefactoringService`: Query optimization and refactoring 3. **Connection Management**: Handles source/destination connections - Supports multiple connector types (GitHub, Salesforce, DuckDB, PostgreSQL) - Schema discovery and mapping ### Frontend Architecture - Built with React + TypeScript + Vite - Uses TanStack Router for routing - TanStack Query for API state management - Tailwind CSS + shadcn/ui for styling - JSON Schema Forms for dynamic connector configuration ### Temporal Workflows The system uses Temporal for reliable distributed workflow execution: - `ConnectionDataSyncWorkflow`: Main sync orchestration - `SyncWorkflow`: Individual sync execution - `DataAgentWorkflow`: Chat processing pipeline - Activities handle atomic operations like API calls, database writes ## Testing Approach - RSpec for Rails API tests with VCR for external API mocking - Vitest for React component and unit tests - Factory Bot for test data generation - Database Cleaner for test isolation ## Environment Variables Key environment variables include: - `TEMPORAL_HOST`, `TEMPORAL_PORT`, `TEMPORAL_NAMESPACE`: Temporal configuration - `DATABASE_URL`: PostgreSQL connection - `REDIS_URL`: DragonflyDB connection (Redis-compatible) - `OPENAI_API_KEY` or `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`: LLM provider credentials - `GITHUB_ACCESS_TOKEN`: For GitHub connector authentication - `SECRET_KEY_BASE`: Rails secret key (required for production) ## DSPy Framework Integration The project is migrating from LangChain to DSPy.rb for structured AI programming: ### DSPy Architecture - **Signatures**: Type-safe input/output definitions using T::Struct and enums - **Modular Services**: Component-based architecture with clear separation of concerns - **Error Handling**: Centralized error management with structured responses - **Type Safety**: Strong typing with Sorbet for better code maintainability ### DSPy Services 1. **ConnectorSelectionServiceV2**: Intelligent ETL connector selection - Analyzes user requirements and recommends optimal connectors - Handles pipeline creation and clarification messages - Components: ConnectorFormatter, PipelineActionHandler, MessageHandler, ErrorHandler 2. **ChatMetadataGeneratorServiceV2**: Enhanced chat processing - Generates comprehensive metadata for chat sessions - Supports complex conversation context and error recovery 3. **QueryRefactoringService**: SQL query optimization - Refactors natural language queries for better execution - Handles complex query patterns and optimization ## Code Style - Ruby: Follow RuboCop configuration (double quotes, frozen string literals) - TypeScript: ESLint + Prettier configuration - Commit messages should be descriptive and follow conventional format - The project consists of: - A Rails API backend (`platform/`) - A React/TypeScript frontend (`ui/`) - Ruby-based data connectors (`ruby_connectors/`) - Temporal workflow orchestration for ETL processes ## Development Commands ### Backend (Rails API) ```bash # From the platform/ directory bundle install # Install Ruby dependencies rails db:create # Create database rails db:migrate # Run migrations rails db:seed # Seed initial data rails server # Start Rails server on port 3000 rails console # Start Rails console # Testing bundle exec rspec # Run all tests bundle exec rspec spec/path/to/spec.rb # Run specific test file # Linting bundle exec rubocop # Run RuboCop linter bundle exec rubocop -a # Auto-fix linting issues ``` ### Frontend (React/TypeScript) ```bash # From the ui/ directory bun install # Install dependencies bun run dev # Start development server bun run build # Build for production bun run test # Run tests bun run coverage # Run tests with coverage bun run lint # Run ESLint bun run pretty # Format code with Prettier ``` ### Ruby Connectors ```bash # From the ruby_connectors/ directory bundle install # Install dependencies bundle exec rspec # Run tests bundle exec rubocop # Run linter ``` ### Docker Development ```bash # From the root directory docker-compose up -d # Start all services (PostgreSQL, DragonflyDB, Temporal, Rails, UI) docker-compose down # Stop all services docker-compose logs -f [service] # View logs docker-compose exec rails bundle exec rails console # Rails console # Production deployment docker-compose -f docker-compose.production.yml up -d ``` ### Temporal Workers ```bash # Rails Temporal worker bundle exec rails temporal:worker # Ruby connectors Temporal worker bundle exec ruby_connectors temporal_worker ``` ## Architecture Overview ### Backend Structure The Rails API follows a service-oriented architecture: - **Controllers**: API endpoints under `app/controllers/api/v1/` - **Services**: Business logic in `app/services/` organized by domain (connections, connectors, syncs, ETL, AI) - **Temporal Workflows**: Orchestration logic in `app/services/temporal/workflows/` - **Temporal Activities**: Individual workflow steps in `app/services/temporal/activities/` - **Models**: ActiveRecord models representing core entities (Connection, Connector, Sync, Chat, etc.) ### Key Services 1. **ETL Pipeline**: Handles data extraction from sources, transformation, and loading to DuckDB - Extractors handle API and database sources - Uses Temporal workflows for orchestration - Implements incremental sync with deduplication 2. **AI/Data Agent**: Chat-based interface for data queries - Uses DSPy.rb for structured AI programming (migrating from LangChain) - Generates SQL queries from natural language - Creates summaries and visualizations - Includes intelligent connector selection service - Key services: - `Ai::Etl::ConnectorSelectionServiceV2`: DSPy-based connector selection - `Ai::ChatMetadataGeneratorServiceV2`: DSPy-based chat metadata generation - `Ai::QueryRefactoringService`: Query optimization and refactoring 3. **Connection Management**: Handles source/destination connections - Supports multiple connector types (GitHub, Salesforce, DuckDB, PostgreSQL) - Schema discovery and mapping ### Frontend Architecture - Built with React + TypeScript + Vite - Uses TanStack Router for routing - TanStack Query for API state management - Tailwind CSS + shadcn/ui for styling - JSON Schema Forms for dynamic connector configuration ### Temporal Workflows The system uses Temporal for reliable distributed workflow execution: - `ConnectionDataSyncWorkflow`: Main sync orchestration - `SyncWorkflow`: Individual sync execution - `DataAgentWorkflow`: Chat processing pipeline - Activities handle atomic operations like API calls, database writes ## Testing Approach - RSpec for Rails API tests with VCR for external API mocking - Vitest for React component and unit tests - Factory Bot for test data generation - Database Cleaner for test isolation ## Environment Variables Key environment variables include: - `TEMPORAL_HOST`, `TEMPORAL_PORT`, `TEMPORAL_NAMESPACE`: Temporal configuration - `DATABASE_URL`: PostgreSQL connection - `REDIS_URL`: DragonflyDB connection (Redis-compatible) - `OPENAI_API_KEY` or `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`: LLM provider credentials - `GITHUB_ACCESS_TOKEN`: For GitHub connector authentication - `SECRET_KEY_BASE`: Rails secret key (required for production) ## DSPy Framework Integration The project is migrating from LangChain to DSPy.rb for structured AI programming: ### DSPy Architecture - **Signatures**: Type-safe input/output definitions using T::Struct and enums - **Modular Services**: Component-based architecture with clear separation of concerns - **Error Handling**: Centralized error management with structured responses - **Type Safety**: Strong typing with Sorbet for better code maintainability ### DSPy Services 1. **ConnectorSelectionServiceV2**: Intelligent ETL connector selection - Analyzes user requirements and recommends optimal connectors - Handles pipeline creation and clarification messages - Components: ConnectorFormatter, PipelineActionHandler, MessageHandler, ErrorHandler 2. **ChatMetadataGeneratorServiceV2**: Enhanced chat processing - Generates comprehensive metadata for chat sessions - Supports complex conversation context and error recovery 3. **QueryRefactoringService**: SQL query optimization - Refactors natural language queries for better execution - Handles complex query patterns and optimization ## Code Style - Ruby: Follow RuboCop configuration (double quotes, frozen string literals) - TypeScript: ESLint + Prettier configuration - Commit messages should be descriptive and follow conventional format - When ever we create a new file named as *.rb file always remember to add *.rb.md explaing the code in detail - Always write the code which is modular, readable, writeable and maintainable - Always Update claude.md when we update the code in a major way # important-instruction-reminders Do what has been asked; nothing more, nothing less. SOURCE: https://github.com/coinbase/temporal-ruby/blob/master/README.md#_snippet_22 LANGUAGE: ruby CODE: ``` class MyWorkflow < Temporal::Workflow def execute ActivityOld1.execute! workflow.sleep(10) ActivityOld2.execute! return nil end end ``` LANGUAGE: ruby CODE: ``` class MyWorkflow < Temporal::Workflow def execute Activity1.execute! if workflow.has_release?(:fix_1) ActivityNew1.execute! end workflow.sleep(10) if workflow.has_release?(:fix_1) ActivityNew2.execute! else ActivityOld.execute! end if workflow.has_release?(:fix_2) ActivityNew3.execute! end return nil end end ``` -------------------------------- TITLE: Add Temporal Ruby Gem to Gemfile DESCRIPTION: This code snippet shows how to include the temporal-ruby gem in your project's Gemfile, specifying that it should be sourced directly from the GitHub repository.
